title: Sheaf Rees algebra
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [pqf-def-coherent]. Use the ideal powers $\mathcal I^0=\mathcal O_X$, $\mathcal I^{n+1}=\mathcal I^n\mathcal I$ of [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] and their canonical associative, unital multiplication maps $\mu_{m,n}:\mathcal I^m\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal I^{m+n}$ [lemma-nagata-sheaf-ideal-powers-assoc], where tensor products are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Define the sheaf Rees algebra by
$$\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n.$$
This is the coproduct (the colimit of the discrete diagram indexed by $\mathbf N$, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with inclusions $\iota_n$. Concretely it is the sheaf of locally finite-support tuples of sections of the $\mathcal I^n$, as in [lem-pur-module-sheaf-coproduct-local-support]. Define its product on homogeneous summands by
$$\iota_m(a)\,\iota_n(b)=\iota_{m+n}(\mu_{m,n}(a\otimes b)),$$
and on locally finite sums by bilinear extension; the associated map from the sheaf tensor product is furnished by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. Its structure morphism and unit are the degree-zero inclusion $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal I^0\xrightarrow{\iota_0}\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I)$. The grading has degree-$n$ summand $\mathcal I^n$, and products add degrees. The associative and unit laws are supplied by [lemma-nagata-sheaf-ideal-powers-assoc]; commutativity is inherited from $\mathcal O_X$. This is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf], and its underlying module is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure]. No injectivity of $\mu_{m,n}$ is assumed.

proof.text: For each $n\in\mathbf N$, take the quasi-coherent ideal power $\mathcal I^n$ of [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Apply [lem-pur-module-sheaf-coproduct-local-support] on the open-set site of $X$ to this countable family. This site is small in the chosen universe and has fibre products given by intersections; module sheafification is supplied by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The result is a specified sheaf $\mathcal R$ of locally finite-support tuples, whose coordinate insertions exhibit the required coproduct in module sheaves. This constructs the underlying object without choosing data from a mere existence claim.

source.place: definition, direct sum in sheaves of modules

proof.text: Use the canonical maps and identities of [lemma-nagata-sheaf-ideal-powers-assoc]. On any open where two tuples have finite support, define their product in degree $k$ by $\sum_{m+n=k}\mu_{m,n}(a_m\otimes b_n)$. Its support is contained in the finite sum of the two support sets. Restriction commutes with this formula since every $\mu_{m,n}$ is a sheaf morphism. The locally finite-support description [lem-pur-module-sheaf-coproduct-local-support] therefore makes the formulas agree on overlaps and glue to a bilinear sheaf pairing. By [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] it gives the specified map $\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R\to\mathcal R$. On a common open with finite supports, the two parenthesized triple products expand into the sums of $\mu_{m+n,r}(\mu_{m,n}(a_m\otimes b_n)\otimes c_r)$ and $\mu_{m,n+r}(a_m\otimes\mu_{n,r}(b_n\otimes c_r))$, respectively. The cited associativity identifies each term. The degree-zero element $1$ is a two-sided unit by the cited unit laws. Swapping $m,n$ and using $ab=ba$ in $\mathcal O_X$ shows commutativity, because the canonical ideal multiplication maps are induced by that product [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Distributivity and scalar compatibility follow termwise from bilinearity. Thus these operations give the stated algebra with its degree-zero structure map; the formula itself shows that multiplication adds degrees.

source.place: definition, homogeneous multiplication and degree-zero unit

proof.text: Each $\mathcal I^n$ is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. The family is indexed by the small set $\mathbf N$, and its underlying module was constructed as its categorical coproduct. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure] to conclude that $\mathcal R$ is quasi-coherent. No finite generation, Noetherian, quasi-compactness, or injectivity hypothesis on multiplication has entered the construction.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. Define
its sheaf Rees algebra by

$$
\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n,
$$

with multiplication induced by the canonical multiplication maps
$\mathcal I^m\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal I^n\to \mathcal I^{m+n}$ and unit the degree-zero copy of $\mathcal O_X$.
The direct sum is taken in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Define
multiplication on homogeneous summands by the displayed maps and extend it
by the universal property of the direct sum; the degree-zero inclusion is
the unit. Associativity and the unit laws are exactly
[lemma-nagata-sheaf-ideal-powers-assoc], so this is a graded
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra. The multiplication maps need not be
injective.
